question.text: Under FCRA 2010, once an NPO is granted FCRA registration, the certificate is valid for a period of ___ years, renewable for a similar term upon application filed at least 6 months before expiry.

explanation.text: The Logic: FCRA registration is valid for 5 years. Renewal applications must be made at least 6 months before the expiry date; delayed applications attract late-fee or rejection risk. Prior permission (one-off) and registration are the two modes of receipt under FCRA. The Trap: 3 years corresponds to Section 12AB provisional (a tax regime), not FCRA. 7 and 10 are fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XXIV (AML) uses KYC periodic-review timelines; XXIII tests FCRA-specific tenures. Do not confuse FCRA renewal (5-year) with FEMA reporting (annual). Assessor's Pro-Tip: At engagement planning, chart the FCRA renewal date alongside 12AB and 80G dates on a compliance calendar. A lapsed FCRA means every subsequent foreign receipt is an offence — and your Annual Impact Report cannot certify a legal receipt if FCRA has expired silently.
